narrative.overview: Context feels like a quiet observatory built from native Apple controls: an abyssal field, sparse stars, warm white information, and one cool signal color. Density stays calm on iPhone and opens up on iPad. Identity comes from the Context mark, the blue page-handoff action, and the recurring floating browser island.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy field with sparse, deterministic stars.
Warm-white content and one sky-blue action color.
Native SwiftUI materials, symbols, Dynamic Type, and device adaptation.
Rounded cards and capsules with quiet one-pixel boundaries.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue identifies actions the user intentionally initiates; it does not decorate passive content.

rules.name: The Quiet Night Rule
rules.body: Stars remain sparse and low contrast.

rules.name: The Native Scale Rule
rules.body: App text uses semantic Dynamic Type roles and must remain useful when the user enlarges text.

rules.name: The Native Layer Rule
rules.body: Use system material when a control floats above web content; use opaque night surfaces when stable contrast matters more than translucency.

dos: Do lead AI-related browsing surfaces with the Context mark and the Signal Blue handoff action.
Do use native iOS symbols, sheets, menus, labels, and Dynamic Type behavior.
Do keep outbound page context reviewable before it leaves the device.
donts: Don't copy Comet branding, illustrations, or screen composition.
Don't add extra accent colors, glossy high-chroma gradients, or dense star effects.
Don't imply that opening Grok Bot automatically sends content or selects a named teammate.
Don't present planned features as available.
